## Which package for which system

* **Ubuntu, x86_64 (.deb)** - every Ubuntu release (the install script picks this build for Ubuntu 18.04 and later and falls back to it for older ones); it also installs on other Debian-family distributions.
* **Debian, x86_64 (.deb)** - every Debian release - the install script picks this build for Debian whatever the version (it is built on Debian 9).
* **Ubuntu, ARM64 / aarch64 (.deb)** - Ubuntu 22.04 and later on ARM64 (the install script refuses older Ubuntu on ARM); published since 6.5.1.
* **RHEL-family and SUSE, x86_64 (.rpm)** - RHEL, CentOS, Rocky, AlmaLinux, Oracle Linux, Amazon Linux, SLES and openSUSE (the install script accepts any distribution whose ID_LIKE says rhel or centos); published since 3.3.1. There is no ARM64 rpm.
* **Windows, x64 (.msi)** - Windows Server and Windows desktops (the Store lists Windows 10 Enterprise and Windows 11 Pro/Enterprise), 64-bit Intel/AMD only. There is no Windows ARM64 build.
* **macOS, Intel (.pkg)** - macOS on Intel Macs (desktops and laptops); published since 2.9.0.
* **macOS, Apple silicon (.pkg)** - macOS on Apple silicon (M-series) Macs; published since 3.1.0.

The packages are the same for servers and desktops: one Windows MSI, one rpm, one deb per architecture, one macOS pkg per architecture. Which operating system releases ServiceNow supports is listed in [Server or desktop](README.md#server-or-desktop) on the index page.

## Change log

Agent Client Collector Framework 7.0.4: Major release, published on the Store 2026-09-10, for the Brazil, Australia, Zurich platform families.

**New**

- Maintenance token for Windows uninstalls: removing an agent needs a token generated for that agent (works offline, audited).
- Official support for non-persistent VDI: agents in a gold image are operational in under 2 minutes, with no duplicate registration when desktops are re-created, no per-desktop TLS certificate, and checks running as soon as the agent connects.

**Changed**

- Upgrade uses a randomised temporary directory (symlink attacks) and the default command allow-list is stricter (privilege escalation).
- Policy refresh processes agents in batches to avoid memory exhaustion on large MIDs.
- Asset metadata is re-published to every active MID after a Framework upgrade.
- Windows picks the host IP from the default-gateway interface first.
- Disabled checks are logged as skipped; a scheduled job cleans up stale checks and resolves their errors.
- Policies support custom CI tables (u_cmdb_ci_*) and are republished in place instead of deleted and recreated.
- Corrupted agent_now_id files are detected and repaired; allow-lists accept JSON5; the WMI permission test works on Windows 11 without wmic.exe.

**Fixed**

- Out-of-memory on policy push with more than 80,000 agents on one MID.
- installed_software hang on RHEL 10 when rpm output exceeded the 64 KB pipe buffer.
- CPU discovery on ARM64 Linux when osquery returns no CPU data.
- Disabled checks reported as running successfully, hiding collection outages.
- Test Check UI hang with more than 28,000 agents; agent crash on YAML parse errors at start.
- Wrong IP on multi-homed Windows hosts; misleading log-fetch error after a successful upgrade.
- MID-less (ICS) agents stuck in Unknown; the duplicate-agent-ID cleanup job running indefinitely; config sync for checks without assets; smaller policy UI and history fixes.

Summarised from ServiceNow's release notes; the full text is on the [Store listing](https://store.servicenow.com/store/app/bc09636e1be06a50a85b16db234bcbd1) under Version details, Release notes.

## Configuration (acc.yml)

Defaults the deb installs as `acc.yml.example`, read from the Ubuntu x86_64 package. On a fresh install the install script copies it to `acc.yml` and fills in `backend-url` and `api-key` (or, MID-less, `instance-url` and `registration-key`); an upgrade keeps the existing `acc.yml`. The Windows MSI carries the same template (byte for byte in 7.1.3) and writes `C:\ProgramData\ServiceNow\agent-client-collector\config\acc.yml`. The rpm ships no template: there `acc.yml` is written by `acc gateway mid` and has no `allow-list:` line. Linux path: `/etc/servicenow/agent-client-collector/acc.yml`.

| Key | Default | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `backend-url` | `wss://127.0.0.1:8800/ws/events` | set |
| `connect-without-mid` | `false` | set |
| `instance-url` | `""` | set |
| `registration-key` | `""` | set |
| `api-key` | `""` | set |
| `log-level` | `info` | set |
| `insecure-skip-tls-verify` | `true` | set |
| `allow-list` | `/etc/servicenow/agent-client-collector/check-allow-list.json` | set |
| `max-running-checks` | `10` | set |
| `agent_cpu_threshold.cpu_percentage_limit` | `5` | set |
| `agent_cpu_threshold.repeated_high_cpu_num` | `3` | set |

Default command allow-list (`check-allow-list.json.default`): 9 entries for 9 commands, 0 of them allowed with any arguments.

Service unit (`acc.service`, deb): User=servicenow, Restart=on-failure, RestartSec=1min, KillMode=control-group, TimeoutStopSec=30.

## Installing

The instance's own install script (served at `/api/sn_agent/agents/install_agent`, Linux and macOS) downloads the right package for the host, verifies its signature, installs it and writes `acc.yml` with the MID endpoint and API key:

```bash
ACC_VERSION=7.0.4 ACC_API_KEY="<api key>" ACC_MID="wss://<mid host>:8800/ws/events" bash -c "$(curl -L https://<instance>.service-now.com/api/sn_agent/agents/install_agent)"
```

By hand, with the package downloaded from the links above:

```bash
sudo dpkg -i agent-client-collector-7.0.4-ubuntu-1804_amd64.deb      # Debian / Ubuntu (use the ARM64 or Debian file on those systems)
sudo rpm -vi agent-client-collector-7.0.4-x86_64.rpm             # RHEL-family / SUSE
sudo installer -target / -pkg agent-client-collector-7.0.4-macos_arm64.pkg   # macOS (Intel: the macos_x64 file)
```

```powershell
msiexec /i agent-client-collector-7.0.4-windows-x64.msi /qn ACC_API_KEY="<api key>" ACC_MID="wss://<mid host>:8800/ws/events"
```

After a manual Linux or macOS install, set `endpoint` and `api-key` in `acc.yml` (`/etc/servicenow/agent-client-collector/acc.yml`) and restart the `acc` service. The Windows MSI takes both as properties.
